summary: We received you letter; thank you. I’ve also heard from Tom Disch, a nice letter, to which I’ve already replied. There is bad news from Poland; Lem writes to say that travel expenses must be paid by us at this end in hard currency. Never­ theless I gave my permission for the Polish edition of UBIK, even though I’ll make nothing out of it... my agent disapproved, but apparently will go along with it. He is right, of course; it is a rip-off. Lem estimates about 10,000 copies. I presume hardcover. His letter is cold and factual and in no way attempts to respond to deeper matters that I wrote about, such as the nature of my current writing. It seemed like something composed by a computer, and turned me off entirely. I had hoped, in my letter to him, to open channels of real communica­ tion, but he talked only about business matters ... and he did not even acknowl­ edge that I had brought up any other topics. I wonder what he will say when he reads my Vancouver speech in S.F. Commentary, which I mentioned to him. Rottensteiner is just about as cold. A bunch of schizoids, without souls. On the other hand, I heard from Bruce Gillespie, a warm fine letter in which he says, “Your letter must be the most powerful polemic against heroin­ pushing that I have ever read. I hope that some of the right people get to read it.” I gave him permission to quote from my very long letter when he publishes my speech, and he said he will. We discussed Disch, both agreeing on Tom’s unique abilities. H...
